answer: Magnetic separators catch ferrous debris in lube oil before it wrecks bearings, much like proof-of-work filters fake-identity nodes by demanding computational heat from every engine room on the river. That brute-force friction imposes a steep fuel cost on any sybil attacker trying to flood the network with ghost accounts. Yet just as heavy sludge can eventually bypass worn filter screens, a massive botnet backed by stolen electricity can overwhelm the core validation kernel if the difficulty target slips.
